subjects.name: ELECTRICAL PUMPS AND VALVES OPERATION SKILL
course_outcomes: Different type of Industrial Pumps and Valves.
Basic electrical parameters measuring instruments
Different type of electrical motor used for pump and valve operation
Different Types of Flow Measurement Devices and electrical transducer used for it.
Different Types of Temperature measurement Devices and electrical transducer used for it.
Different Types of Pressure measurement Devices and electrical transducer used for it

allSyllabusUnits.title: Pumps
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of pumps and basic technology related to operation, operating practice of reciprocating pumps, Positive displacement pump, centrifugal pump, rotary pumps, Measurement of various electrical quantities and application of various electrical measuring instruments. Construction and operation of electrical motor used for all above pump application.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Valves
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of valves and basic technology related to operation and working, of Isolation valve, regulating valve, back flow prevention valve, pressure relief valve, gate valve, globe valve, ball valve and diapharm valve Working, construction and operation of electrical motor and control system used for various valve.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Flow measurement
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of flow measurement devices, basic technology related to measurement. Operating practice of venturi meter, orifice meter, rotameter, pitot-tube Working, construction and operation of electrical transducer used for flow measurement devices

allSyllabusUnits.title: Temperature measurement devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Working and operating practice of Thermometer, Thermocouple, Thermistors, Thermowell and Pyrometer. Working, construction and operation of electrical transducer used for temperature measurement devices

allSyllabusUnits.title: Pressure measurement devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Working and operating practice of U-tube manometer, Inclined tube Manometer, Pressure gauge. Working, construction and operation of electrical transducer used for pressure measurement devices Total Hours 56

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half: Pumps; Valves; Flow measurement

subjects.name: ENGINEERING DRAWING
course_outcomes: Construct basic and intermediate geometry.
To expand their technical communication skill.
Interpret engineering drawings using fundamental technical mathematics.
To recognize and know the resolutions and the methods of engineering drawing.
To advance their visualization skills so that they can apply these skills in emerging new products.
Understand the theory of projection.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Engineering Curves
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Overview to Engineering Graphics and Introduction of engineering curves, Classification & application of Engineering Curves, Construction of Conics-Construction of Ellipse by arc of circle method, Concentric Circle Method, Rectangle Method, Oblong Method, PARABOLA-Rectangle Method,Method of Tangents ( Triangle Method), HYPERBOLA-Rectangular Hyperbola, Directrix ± focus Method for Ellipse, Parabola and Hyperbola with tangent and normal, Cycloidal Curves- Cycloid with tangent and normal, Epi Cycloid and Hypo Cycloid with tangent and normal, Involutes & Spirals along with normal and tangent

allSyllabusUnits.title: Projection of Points and Lines
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to principal planes of projections & Projections of the points located in same quadrant and different quadrants, Projections of line with its inclination to one reference plane, Projections of line with its inclination to two reference planes, Problems of line inclined to two reference planes, True length and inclination with the reference planes, True length and inclination with the reference planes - Problems, True length and inclination with the reference planes - Problems

allSyllabusUnits.title: Projection of planes
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction of different types of plane and overview of projection of plane, Projections of planes (polygons, circle and ellipse) with its inclination to one reference plane, Problems of projection of planes inclined to one reference plane, Projections of planes (polygons, circle and ellipse) with its inclination to one reference plane, Problems, Concept of auxiliary plane method for projections of the plane, Problems

allSyllabusUnits.title: Orthographic Projections
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Fundamental of projection with classification, Principal planes of projection,, Projections from the pictorial view of the object on the principal planes for view from front, top and sides using first angle projection method and third angle projection method, Problems of orthographic projections, Problems of orthographic projections, Full sectional view., Problems of sectional view

allSyllabusUnits.title: Overview to Engineering Graphics
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Drawing instruments and accessories, Use drawing instruments and materials effectively, Follow and apply standard practice as per B.I.S. for planning and layout, choose appropriate scale factor for the drawing as per given situation, Write annotations on a drawing where ever necessary. Choose appropriate line and dimensioning style for a given geometrical entity, Develop the skill to draw polygons, circles and lines with different geometric situations. Use of plane scales and R. F.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Isometric Projections and Isometric View or Drawing
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Isometric Scale, Conversion of orthographic views into isometric projection, isometric view or drawing Total Hours 28

subjects.name: ENVIRONMENT CONSERVATION & DISASTER MANAGEMENT
course_outcomes: Understand the ecosystem and its terminology and solve various engineering problems by applying ecosystem knowledge to produce eco friendly products
Understand the various types of pollutions and their remedial measures
Understand different renewable energy resources and their applications
Understand the role of an engineer concerning climate change and disaster management

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction of Environmental Science
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition of environment, ecosystem, food chain, and food web, he necessity of environmental science, Importance of environment and scope

allSyllabusUnits.title: Types of pollution with their causes, effects and remedial
allSyllabusUnits.topics: measures Air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution, and soil pollution, Global environment problems with their causes, effects & remedies: climate change

allSyllabusUnits.title: Renewable Sources of Energy
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Solar energy: basics of solar energy and its importance, Wind energy: need, limitations and future scope, Recent trends of renewable sources of energy

allSyllabusUnits.title: Disaster Management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Concepts and definition of disaster, Disaster management cycle, ole of an engineer in disaster management Rescue techniques during a disaster, Natural disasters: earthquake, cyclone, flood, tsunami, drought, and landslides, Manmade disaster: fire, civil war, technological disasters Total Hours 28

subjects.name: GENERATIVE AI & PROMPT ENGINEERING
course_outcomes: Apply the basic working principles of Generative AI to identify suitable engineering applications.
Use appropriate AI tools to perform specific engineering tasks effectively.
Construct structured and optimized prompts for solving engineering problems.
Examine and refine AI-generated outputs to improve correctness and usefulness.
Develop prompt-based solutions to handle real-world engineering workflows.

allSyllabusUnits.title: AI IN ENGINEERING PRACTICE
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Basics of Generative AI, AI working principle (prediction concept), AI vs Traditional tools, AI tools overview, Engineering applications of AI

allSyllabusUnits.title: SMART USE OF AI TOOLS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Communication with AI, AI tool capabilities & limitations, Tool selection for tasks, Common usage mistakes, Data privacy & confidentiality, Safety considerations, Bias and incorrect outputs

allSyllabusUnits.title: PROMPT DESIGN FUNDAMENTALS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to prompts and Prompt structure (task, context, format), Types of prompts, Step-by-step prompting, Problem decomposition, Example-based prompting, Prompt templates (report, checklist, SOP)

allSyllabusUnits.title: PRACTICAL ENGINEERING APPLICATIONS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Inspection applications, Maintenance applications, Safety applications, Work planning, Structured output generation, Prompt refinement, Output comparison, Workflow prompting

allSyllabusUnits.title: AI-ASSISTED EVALUATION AND ETHICS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Using AI Tools for Code Generation, Code Debugging and Optimization, Prompt Chaining for Step-by-step Development, Detecting Hallucinations in AI-generated Code, Responsible AI Usage, Data Privacy and Security Considerations, Mini Project using Python and Prompt Engineering Total Hours 0

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half: AI IN ENGINEERING PRACTICE; SMART USE OF AI TOOLS; PROMPT DESIGN FUNDAMENTALS

subjects.name: INTEGRATED PERSONALITY DEVELOPMENT COURSE-I
course_outcomes: 1. To provide students with a holistic value-based education that will enable them to be successful in their academic, professional, and social lives.
2. To give the students the tools to develop effective habits, promote personal growth, and improve their well being, stability, and productivity.
3. To allow students to establish a stronger connection with their family through critical thinking and development of qualities such as unity, forgiveness, empathy, and effective communication.
4. To provide students with soft skills that complement their hard skills, making them more marketable when entering the workforce.
5. To enhance awareness of India s glory and global values, and to create considerate citizens who strive for the betterment of their family, college, workforce, and nation.
6. To inspire students to strive for a higher sense of character by learning from role models who have lived principled, disciplined, and value-based lives.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Remaking Yourself Restructuring Yourself
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students learn how self-improvement enables them to secure a bright future for themselves. They will learn 6 powerful thought- processes that can develop their intellectual, physical, emotional, and spiritual quotients.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Remaking Yourself Power of Habit
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will undergo a study of how habits work, the habits of successful professionals, and the practical techniques that can be used to develop good habits in their life.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Learning from Legends- Tendulkar & Tata
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn from the inspirational lives of India's two legends, Sachin Tendulkar and Ratan Tata. They will implement these lessons through relatable case studies.

allSyllabusUnits.title: From House to Home Listening & Understanding
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Active listening is an essential part of academic progress and communications. Students will learn to listen with their eyes, ears, mind, and heart.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Welcoming Challenges
allSyllabusUnits.topics: This lecture enables students to revisit the way in which they approach challenges. Through the study of successful figures such as Disney, Lincoln and Bachchan, students will learn to face difficulties through a positive perspective.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Significance of Failures
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Failure is a student¶s daily source of fear, negativity, and depression. Students will be given the constructive skills to understand failure as formative learning experiences.

allSyllabusUnits.title: My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-1
allSyllabusUnits.topics: India¶s ancient Rishis, scholars, and intellectuals have made tremendous contributions to the world, they developed an advanced, sophisticated culture and civilization which began thousands of years ago. Students will learn the importance of studying India¶s glorious past so that they could develop a strong passion and pride for our nation.

allSyllabusUnits.title: My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-2
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Our ancient concepts can be used to seek revolutionary ideas and to generate inspiration. Students will develop a deeper interest in India¶s Glorious Past ± by appreciating the need to read about it, research it, write about it, and share it.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Learning from Legends A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Dr Kalam¶s inspirational life displayed legendary qualities which apply to students (1) Dare to Dream (2) Work Hard (3) Get Good Guidance (4) Humility (5) Use Your Talents for the Benefit of Others

allSyllabusUnits.title: Soft Skills Networking & Leadership
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students are taught the means of building a professional network and developing a leadership attitude.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Soft Skills Project Management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn the secrets of project management through the Akshardham case study. They will then practice these skills through an activity relevant to student life.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Remaking Yourself Handling Social Media
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn how social media can become addictive and they will imbibe simple methods to take back control.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Power of Faith
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn about the power and necessity of faith in our daily lives.

allSyllabusUnits.title: From House to Home Bonding the Family
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will understand the importance of strong family relationships. They will learn how to overcome the generation gap and connect with their family more.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Selfless Service Seva
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn that performing seva is beneficial to one¶s health, wellbeing, and happiness. It also benefits and inspires others. Total Hours 30

subjects.name: MATHEMATICS-II
course_outcomes: Learn concept of Matrix and Determinant and solve the system of linear equations by using matrix.
Solve equations of algebraic expressions using algebraic skills.
Solve the problems using functions.
Solve the problem of function using the concept of Limit.
Find the nth term and Sum of arithmetic and geometric progression.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Determinants and Matrices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Algebra of Matrices, Determinant of Matrix, Inverse of Matrix up to 3×3 matrix, Solution of Simultaneous Equation (up to 3 variable)

allSyllabusUnits.title: Equations
allSyllabusUnits.topics: System of Linear Equation, Solution of Quadratic Equation, Solution of Cubic Equation

allSyllabusUnits.title: Function
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction of Function, Algebra of Function, Example of Function

allSyllabusUnits.title: Limit of functions
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition and some properties of limits, Limit of polynomial and rational functions, Limit of trigonometric function, Limit of exponential function, Limit at infinity

allSyllabusUnits.title: Arithmetic and Geometric Progression
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Nth term of A.P, Sum of first N terms of A.P, Nth term of G.P, Sum of first N terms of G.P Total Hours 28

subjects.name: UNIT OPERATION-I
course_outcomes: Understand different properties of particulate solids and methods of out its analysis.
Express criteria for selection of specific size reduction equipments based on their application.
Be able to utilize theoretical knowledge for fundamental design of suitable solid liquid separation operation
To build a bridge between theoretical and practical concepts of unit operation used in chemical industry to solve environmental pollution problems.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Particulate Solids
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Particle characterization, Concept of sphericity, Mixed particles size, specific surface area and specific number of particles Basic terms in screening, Screen analysis- differential and cumulative analysis.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Size Reduction and Screening
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Crushing Law, Classification of size reduction equipments, Crushers, Grinders, Ultra-fine grinders, Cutting machines, Open circuit and closed circuit operation, Screen effectiveness, Ideal screen and actual screen, Different screening equipments

allSyllabusUnits.title: Filtration, Sedimentation and Centrifugal Separation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition and Mechanisms of filtration, Filtration theory, Filter media and filter aids, Classification & Selection of filtration equipments, Bag filter in air pollution control, Plate and frame filter press, Rotary drum filter etc. Batch sedimentation test, Applications of sedimentation, Theory of centrifugal separation, centrifugal filtration, Classification of centrifuges, Simple bowl centrifuge, Disc centrifuge, Tubular-bowl centrifuge, Gas centrifuge

allSyllabusUnits.title: Solid-Solid and Solid-Fluid Separation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Magnetic Separation, Froth Floatation, Cyclone Separation and Electrostatic Precipitation Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half: Particulate Solids; Size Reduction and Screening; Filtration, Sedimentation and Centrifugal Separation

Questions: [8 marks] Explain Engineering curves and their practical classification. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Constructing an ellipse by standard geometric methods. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Parabola and hyperbola construction and the focus/directrix idea. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Cycloidal curves, involutes and spirals. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
Engineering curves include conics and other geometric curves used to represent shapes or motion. Ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas are conic sections; cycloids, epicycloids, hypocycloids, involutes and spirals are other common constructions in engineering graphics. The method is chosen according to the defining geometry and the intended use. A drawing should show construction lines clearly, use suitable instruments and identify the required tangent or normal when requested. Accuracy depends on the construction procedure and neat, unambiguous line work.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
An ellipse can be constructed by methods such as concentric circles, rectangle or oblong methods, and arc-of-circle approaches taught in the syllabus. First mark the major and minor axes and their centres accurately. Divide the relevant circles, sides or arcs into corresponding parts, project matching points and draw a smooth continuous curve through them. Select the method according to the data and construction requested. Check symmetry about both axes and use light construction lines before darkening the final curve.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A conic is defined by a geometric relation between a point and a focus/directrix or by another specified construction condition. A parabola has eccentricity one; an ellipse has eccentricity below one and a hyperbola above one. Construction methods use the given dimensions or geometric properties to locate successive points, then join them smoothly. Tangents and normals are drawn according to the prescribed method at the required point. Verify the defining dimensions and symmetry and distinguish the conics by their geometry rather than by appearance alone.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A cycloid is traced by a point on a circle rolling along a straight line. An epicycloid is generated when a circle rolls outside another circle, while a hypocycloid is generated when it rolls inside. An involute can be understood as the path traced by the end of a taut string unwound from a base curve; spirals move progressively inward or outward according to their construction. Start from the generating geometry, divide the motion into corresponding steps, plot points carefully and construct any requested tangent or normal.

Engineering curves include conics and other geometric curves used to represent shapes or motion. The method is chosen according to the defining geometry and the intended use. A drawing should show construction lines clearly, use suitable instruments and identify the required tangent or normal when requested. Accuracy depends on the construction procedure and neat, unambiguous line work.

Answers:
Model answer:
A drawing sheet should have a suitable size, border, title block and layout, with space allocated for views and notes. Instruments such as drawing boards, T-squares or parallel rules, set squares, compass, divider and scale support accurate construction. Standard line conventions distinguish visible outlines, hidden edges, centre lines, dimensions and construction work. Use lettering and dimensioning consistently and choose a suitable scale when the object will not fit at full size. Standards make drawings legible and interpretable by others, rather than relying on informal assumptions.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Representative fraction (RF) is drawing length divided by actual length after both are expressed in the same units. A full-size scale has RF 1:1; a reducing scale has RF below one, and an enlarging scale has RF greater than one. For example, RF 1:5 means a 50 mm actual length is shown as 10 mm on the drawing. Select a scale that preserves legibility and available sheet space, state it clearly, and apply it consistently to dimensions and construction. The written dimension normally states actual size, not the measured paper length.

Model answer:

Choose line types according to their purpose: visible outlines, hidden details, centre lines and dimension lines should be distinguishable. Annotations should be placed near the relevant feature without clutter. A drawing should contain enough dimensions to manufacture or inspect the part, but not contradictory or redundant values. Apply the relevant standard conventions and check units and overall dimensions.

Model answer:
Orthographic projection represents an object through views perpendicular to principal planes. The front view communicates height and width, the top view width and depth, and a side view height and depth. In first-angle projection, the object is between the observer and projection plane; in third-angle projection, the projection plane is between observer and object. Therefore the arrangement of views differs. Identify the projection method by its symbol or stated convention, align corresponding dimensions across views, and check that the set of views describes one consistent object.
